title: Make a Habit of Learning English

source.name: VOA Learning English — Make a Habit of Learning English
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Since the beginning of the coronavirus crisis, many people have had to change their habits, or usual ways of doing things.
Some people who used to go to school now study at home. Some of them have been trying to get in the habit of learning and studying on their own.
Habits are regular ways of dealing with your environment. You generally do not pay attention to them.
Habits take many forms – eating, exercising, even studying. You may not realize it, but habits make up many of the actions that you do every day.
In the book Atomic Habits , James Clear describes a four-step process by which habits are made. These steps are cue, craving, response, and reward.

The cue tells your brain to begin a behavior. The craving is what makes you want to do something. The response is the actual habit that you perform. The response, in turn, gives you a reward. “Rewards are the end goal of every habit,” Clear writes.

Consider this example. Maybe you have the habit of often checking social media. The cue might be a feeling of boredom while you are near your computer or phone. The craving could be a desire to stop that feeling. The response is checking social media, and the reward is seeing something interesting. When that process is repeated many times, it becomes a habit.

You should organize your surroundings in such a way that the cues of your new habit are very obvious. For example, if you want to get in the habit of studying English every day, leave English books or notes in a very clear place.

To make your habit attractive, Clear recommends joining a culture where your new desired behavior is the normal behavior. For example, you could join a group of other English learners in online meetings.

To make your new habit easy, you could decrease the number of steps you have to take in order to study. You could also try reducing the amount of time you study. Clear suggests beginning your habits with limited, shorter time periods – two minutes for example. As you repeat the practice over time, you can go longer.
An important point to keep in mind is that if you place too many demands on yourself, you are more likely to give up on your new habit.

Finally, you need to make your habit satisfying. You can give yourself a reward after completing your new habit. For example, if you study English for 15 minutes, you could reward yourself by listening to a song you like. Or you could think about how much progress you have made since you first started studying English.
Building new habits can take time. You may have to repeat an action many times before it becomes a habit. But with time, careful planning and continued practice, you can do it.

questions.q: Why do people often fail to notice their own habits?
options: They carry them out almost without thinking
Habits appear suddenly during a crisis
They only happen when people are bored
People forget what they did the day before
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: thói quen là cách quen thuộc đối phó với môi trường và “You generally do not pay attention to them” ≈ làm gần như không nghĩ.

questions.q: In the social-media example, what is the “craving”?
options: Finding something interesting to read
The feeling of boredom itself
The act of looking at the screen
A wish to get rid of a bored feeling
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: cue = cảm giác chán; craving = mong muốn chấm dứt cảm giác đó; response = lướt mạng; reward = thấy điều thú vị.

questions.q: Which suggestion would help make a new study habit “obvious”?
options: Beginning with study sessions of only two minutes each day
Joining an online group of other learners of the English language
Leaving your English notes where you will see them every day
Listening to a favourite song as a reward after studying
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: làm cue rõ ràng → để sách/ghi chú ở chỗ dễ thấy. Nhóm online = attractive; hai phút = easy; nghe bài hát = satisfying.

questions.q: Why does Clear suggest starting with very short study sessions?
options: Longer sessions are never useful for learners, however much time they have
Small beginnings are easier to keep up, and you can lengthen them later
The brain cannot learn anything new when a lesson lasts longer than two minutes
Teachers say that short lessons are always better than long ones
questions.explain: Đoạn 10–11: bắt đầu với thời gian ngắn (ví dụ hai phút) để dễ làm, sau đó tăng; đòi hỏi quá nhiều làm dễ bỏ cuộc.

questions.q: In paragraph 11, “place too many demands on yourself” most nearly means
options: spend too much money on study materials
compare yourself with other learners
ask other people to help you
expect too much from yourself
questions.explain: Đoạn 11: “if you place too many demands on yourself, you are more likely to give up” ≈ kì vọng/đặt yêu cầu quá cao ở bản thân.

questions.q: Being part of a group where your new behaviour is normal can make a habit more attractive.
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: Clear khuyên tham gia “a culture where your new desired behavior is the normal behavior”.

questions.q: Studying in online meetings is more effective than studying with a group in person.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nêu họp trực tuyến như một ví dụ; không so sánh với học trực tiếp.
